title: Opinion on how long rock and roll will last
summary: Miller says rock and roll's noise will be knocked out, while Dixieland and the blues remain standard.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah, Alexander's Ragtime Band. He really played that. But Dick, what I want to ask you, what do you think about how long you think Rock and Roller lasts?
Oh, I don't know. It can't last much longer.

Well, in my mind, the way I figured out, if any little thing different come in with, I mean it got to be noisy, got to be flashy, you know, stuff. It'll knock it out. But Cha Cha ain't going to knock it out.

Not that. See Cha Cha is good music, but it ain't got no, what these young people wanted, that noise and stuff and flashy stuff, you see. That's what killed them off, see. Of course, Dixieland, don't care what come out, he's going to hang around, you know, and it might get famous again. Of course, Dixieland is a standard kind of music, you know, a standard.
Well, there'll always be people playing the blues, I figure.
Oh, as long as you live there. See, Rock and Roll ain't got butt blues.
